title: EU leaders wrestle over Ukraine aid as potential Le Pen victory sparks fear
summary_full: Slovakia, Hungary and Czechia want to opt out of €45bn Ukraine loan, as Germany tries to protect funding from possible far-right French presidencyEurope live – latest updatesEU leaders were bracing for a clash over long-term financial aid for Ukraine amid an effort to finalise high-stakes budget talks by the end of the year.Arriving in Brussels on Thursday, the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, reiterated his view that all EU member states should support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine for 2027. “When the European Union provides funding, it does so as the European Union – and that union consists of 27 member states, not 23 or 24,” he said.
